settings.title: Custom formulation
settings.body: We own the formulas and the plant. When the shelf product does not fit your water, your surface or your soil, our chemists change it — from one pallet. Nobody who buys from a distributor can say that.

settings.title: Enzyme technology
settings.body: Live biological chemistry for drains, traps, odor and organic soil — the part of the line that keeps working long after the crew clocks out.

settings.title: Equipment & grant experts
settings.body: Autoscrubbers, dispensers, laundry and foaming systems specced to the building — plus people on staff who write the grant that pays for them.

settings.title: Mobile repair
settings.body: Techs and parts come to your facility. Any brand, including equipment we never sold you. Preventive plans so the floor machine does not die mid‑shift.

settings.title: The Q Team
settings.body: Chemists, service techs, grant writers and inside sales, listed by name and specialty. One phone number, and the person who can change the formula is down the hall.

settings.title: Private label
settings.body: Your label, your contact info, your dilution chart, our chemistry. Artwork approval to shipment in three to four weeks, one pallet minimum.

settings.heading: Six things we do that a distributor cannot.
settings.description: Each of these is a full page on the new site. The homepage's only job is to make you realize we do it at all.

settings.title: Enzyme program, not another fragrance
settings.body: Fragrance masks for four hours. A dosed enzyme program digests the organic film in the drain line and the trap so the smell stops being generated in the first place. We start with a two‑week trial on your worst line.

settings.title: Concentrate plus the right dispenser
settings.body: Hoods, fryers and rotisserie carbon are a chemistry‑and‑dilution problem. We spec the concentrate to your soil, then mount a dilution station so your crew stops free‑pouring at four times the cost.

settings.title: Floor program with the machine included
settings.body: Finish, stripper and daily neutral cleaner specced against your substrate — then the autoscrubber sized to your square footage, installed, trained and serviced by our techs.

settings.title: Documented kill claims and the binder to prove it
settings.body: EPA‑registered chemistry with the dwell times your surveyor will ask about, plus an auto‑assembled SDS and registration binder for the products on your account.

settings.title: Mobile repair first, replacement second
settings.body: Before you buy, our tech comes to the building and looks at what you have — any brand. Most machines we see are one part and a calibration away from another two years.

settings.problem_label: No capital budget for what we need
settings.title: Start with the grant, not the quote
settings.body: Our grant people check which cycles are open for your entity type, tell you honestly whether you qualify, and help write the equipment into the narrative. We have done this paperwork before.

settings.title: A formula built for one customer — yours
settings.body: Roughly a third of what leaves our dock was built for a single account. Tell the chemist the surface, the soil and the water; we blend against it and you can have it under your own label.

settings.subheading: Not a product search. Two questions and you land on the person who has solved this before — with the chemistry, the equipment and the funding angle already attached.

settings.title: Safer on the crew

settings.heading: Biology does the work after your crew goes home.
settings.lead: A surfactant cleans what you can reach. Enzymes keep working down the drain line, in the grease trap, under the tile, in the mop bucket — digesting the organic soil that causes the odor instead of perfuming over it. It is the least understood thing we make and the most defensible.

settings.title: Installed, trained, maintained

settings.title: Grant experts on staff
settings.body: Ohio EPA, ESSER successors, USDA Rural Development, state school‑facility funds. Our people know which cycle is open, what the narrative needs to say, and how to write the equipment into it.
